_comment: Golden vectors for the signed receipt wire format. EVERY producer and
verifier must reproduce these exactly, in whatever language it is written.
This file is the shared safety mechanism named in the receipt contract:
the ecosystem deliberately runs several INDEPENDENT implementations
(gNode daemon in Rust, Geodineum-COMMS in Rust, and the polyglot clients
of SB-8.88 in Python/C/TypeScript), so nothing but a common set of test
vectors keeps them from drifting apart. A drift is invisible in normal
operation and then presents as a signature failure, which reads as
tampering rather than as a regression.
Ed25519 is deterministic (RFC 8032): a fixed seed over fixed input has
exactly one correct signature, so these values are stable forever.
Copies live in gNode, Geodineum-COMMS and Geodineum-pro/CONTRACTS and
canonical_bytes_utf8:
v=1
alg=ed25519
cid=req-1
cmd=cmd
st=ok
e=
ss=site
sn=node
ts=42
bref=ref
bh=230d8358dc8e8890b4c58deeb62912ee2f20357ae92a5cc861b98e68fe31acb5
pid=
fid=
canonical_bytes_note: Field order is part of the signature. Absent optionals (error/parent_id/flow_id) render as the EMPTY STRING, not as an omitted line — a verifier that skips the line computes different bytes and rejects exactly the healthy receipts.
